unit.why: A halakhic discussion of the fasts imposed on a woman whose child died beside her, built around an anecdote: such a woman came before the Apter rav, and he recalls arguing the point in his youth at a gathering of elders in Zlotchov, where all accepted his view.
unit.boundary_note: The closing words 'מענין אתרוג' are the section heading of the next division.

stories.start_quote: איתא בפסקי ה״ג ז״ל אשה שמצאה
stories.end_quote: בא וראה החכמה תחיה את בעליה
stories.summary_en: The Apter rav rules that a woman who found her baby dead beside her should redeem her penitential fasts with money instead of fasting, because fasting would harm future pregnancies. He recounts that in his youth he made this argument at a gathering of elders in Zlotchov against the local rabbi's strict ruling, and everyone agreed with him.

Penitential fasts and their reduction are the subject.
